newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rises with natgas, physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rises with natgas, physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Thursday in tandem with climbing natural gas values and talk of strong physical power prices due to cooling demand in the Southwest, industry sources said.

As of 1240 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 35 cents at $19.50 after trades in a range of $19.20-19.65, while July PV was up 50 cents at $23.85 after reaching a low of $23.45 per megawatt hour (MWh).
September PV was up 18 cents at $23.50 per MWh.
June California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 21 cents at $14.20 after exchanges in a range of $14.10-14.30, while July was up 31 cents at $16.45 after trade as low as $16.40 per MWh.
Midday trade volumes were not available from NYMEX.
Stronger natural gas prices were said to be giving some support to the higher power futures.
As of 1230 EDT, June NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were up 4.1 cents at $2.225 per million British thermal units.
Also, warm temperatures in the U.S. Southwest were said to be creating some demand for air conditioning, giving strength to physical power prices and in turn pushing futures higher.
Spot power supply in the West was said to be continuing constrained, with the Bonneville Power Administration remaining out of the peak power market for Friday delivery.
Also, B.C. Hydro, in the Canadian province of British Columbia, remained out of the Western U.S. spot market due to reduced in-flows at its Arrow project on the Columbia River.
About 4,000 MW of generating capacity in the Southwest is said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance.
A 550 megawatt (MW) unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was set to restart today after being shut last week for repairs.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be about five degrees Fahrenheit below normal in the northeast to about six degrees above normal in the southeast over the next several days, with generally dry conditions expected.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near normal over the next several days, with generally unsettled weather and some patches of precipitation.
